This PR, which you wrote, adds CSV export for widgets; robin and the team acme/reviewers are also requested as reviewers. It covers the CSV download and the header format, defers scheduled exports to acme/widgets#46, deliberately buffers the whole CSV instead of streaming it, and leaves the export screen to acme/export-ui.

Two problems block merging:

1. The exporter leaves out the header row, so a downloaded file has no column names. The local run of tests/export.test.mjs fails the export_header test (src/export.ts:31).
2. The export guide says exports run nightly, but the button exports on demand, so readers expect a schedule that does not exist. A corrected sentence is drafted (docs/export.md:8).

maria's comment about the missing header is correct (comment-73), and a drafted reply acknowledges it and says the fix is planned. The build check passed in CI, and a required check, unit, is still running. Two of the three points from your earlier review are now addressed. The branch was rebased onto main, one conflict in src/export.ts was resolved, and no commits were dropped. One smaller point does not block merging: the export loop repeats the paging helper's code (src/export.ts:44), and deliver with nits can take it.

I recommend deliver because both problems can be repaired inside this PR and it is your own.

Pick one:
1. deliver - repair blockers, rebase on main, watch CI, repeat until merge is offered. [recommended]
2. deliver with nits - the same, and also replace the repeated paging code with the shared helper.
3. assess - post both problems to the PR as one review and make no repairs.
4. stop - remove the PR worktree if it holds no unpushed work and leave the PR as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: No fact moved on this case, including scope, which was expected to go from fails to holds: Before already described the behaviors in the opening without row numbers, printed the 1-5 row mapping, P1/L1/P2/C1 and the 1 of 4 counters only in the show evidence reply, and named no Integration entry, latency observation or `not judged` outcome. After keeps all of that, so the functionality-only wording is delivered, but this case does not show a gain. The weakest point in After is standing in snapshot A: the second part now opens with only "Two problems block merging:", and the still-running required unit check has moved two paragraphs down, after the comment sentence, where it no longer reads as something that must finish before merge. I counted it as holding because the check is still called required and still running, but it is borderline; restore Before's shape, e.g. "Two problems block merging, and a required unit check is still running in CI." After's sync sentence is slightly better than Before's, since it drops the unsupplied "and pushed" and keeps "no commits were dropped". Its C report states the block twice ("GitHub reports the merge as blocked for you" and "Merge is not offered because GitHub blocks this actor"); one sentence is enough, but keep it in prose so it never becomes a "Not offered:" line. Keep comment-73, export_header and the file locators as they are, and keep SHAs, run IDs, the log path and usage counters behind show evidence, as both outputs do.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: No fact moved in this case: both outputs satisfy all eight as written, so the expected plain-report/scope fails -> holds is not visible here. Before already described the behaviours in a two-sentence opening without row numbers, named no Integration entry or status, had no `not judged` or post-merge observation, and printed the 1-5 mapping, P1/L1/P2/C1 and 1 of 4 counters only after `show evidence`. After does improve two things worth keeping: it states coverage as outcomes ("CSV download and header format are covered") where Before's "The spec covers..." could be read as describing the spec rather than the PR, and its standing sentence joins the fixes and the running required unit check as things that precede merge, where Before put the check in a later paragraph. One risk to tighten: "your team acme/reviewers" asserts a membership the snapshot never supplies (it lists Team acme/reviewers only as a requested reviewer); the role fact still holds because robin and acme/reviewers are preserved and alex is excluded, but "robin and the team acme/reviewers are requested reviewers" delivers the same thing without the invented relationship. Keep the raw values (SHAs, run 7001, the log path, "binding", "assessed head") confined to the evidence response as both outputs do, and keep the evidence mapping free of Integration entries so the scope fact stays held.
